concepts.why: The presence of multiple asymptomatic, skin-colored nodules and a nodule on the lateral tongue, which have slowly increased in size and number, is consistent with cysticercosis, a parasitic infection caused by the pork tapeworm.

The presence of multiple discrete, firm, freely mobile nodules, including one on the lateral tongue, is consistent with neurofibromatosis type 1, a genetic disorder that can cause neurofibromas to develop on the skin and other tissues.

The presence of multiple firm, freely mobile nodules that have slowly increased in size and number is consistent with fibromatosis, a condition characterized by the growth of fibrous tissue in the skin and other tissues.

The presence of multiple discrete, firm, freely mobile nodules is consistent with lipomatosis, a condition characterized by the growth of multiple lipomas, which are benign tumors composed of fat tissue.
The presence of discrete, firm, freely mobile nodules without overlying erythema, warmth, or tenderness is consistent with dermatofibroma, a common benign skin tumor.

The presence of multiple skin-colored nodules, which have slowly increased in size and number, and normal laboratory investigations, including lipid profiles, is consistent with eruptive xanthoma, a condition characterized by the growth of xanthomas, which are benign tumors composed of lipid-laden cells.
The presence of discrete, firm, freely mobile nodules without overlying erythema, warmth, or tenderness is consistent with histocytoma, a type of benign skin tumor composed of histiocytes.
The presence of multiple firm, freely mobile nodules that have slowly increased in size and number is consistent with sclerotic fibroma, a type of benign skin tumor composed of fibrous tissue.

concepts.why: The presence of multiple skin-colored nodules, including one on the lateral tongue, is consistent with lipoid proteinosis, a rare genetic disorder characterized by the deposition of lipoproteins in the skin and other tissues.

The presence of multiple firm, freely mobile nodules that have slowly increased in size and number is consistent with fibrolipomatosis, a condition characterized by the growth of fibrolipomas, which are benign tumors composed of fibrous and fatty tissue.

rationales.F01: Multiple asymptomatic skin-colored nodules are consistent with cysticercosis and dermatofibroma.
rationales.F04: Discrete, firm, freely mobile nodules are consistent with cysticercosis, dermatofibroma, and fibromatosis.
rationales.F06: A nodule on the lateral tongue is highly suggestive of cysticercosis.
rationales.F09: Negative serologic tests for HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C viruses make cysticercosis less likely.
rationales.F11: The absence of neurologic symptoms makes neurofibromatosis type 1 less likely.
